title: Phased release containment and expedited patch pipeline for tenant-impacting inference regressions
creator: Alexandra Chen
description:
Summary: A subset of recent model rollouts produced inference regressions visible in production across Hosted and Dedicated customers and one Private deployment. This ticket codifies an operational containment plan and an expedited patch pipeline to reduce blast radius, restore acceptable quality for affected tenants, and harmonize rollback vs patch decisions across deployment modes.

Goals:
- Rapidly isolate affected tenant slices and minimize customer-visible errors.
- Provide a repeatable decision checklist: revert (full rollback), tenant-pin (targeted remediation), or forward-fix (hotpatch) with safety gates.
- Ship a validated hotfix pipeline that runs lightweight acceptance suites against tenant slices before re-opening traffic.
- Improve post-incident telemetry so future detection thresholds map directly to automated containment actions.

Scope: Hosted API, Dedicated pools (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem) customers. Work includes orchestration playbook, automation scripts, monitoring dashboards, PR template for hotfixes, and a communications checklist for SRE/Support/Account teams.
steps: Triage: confirm regression signature and affected model versions using model-release metadata and trace-id sampling
Slice isolation: create tenant slice in routing (traffic-tag) and divert to fallback model variant or stub endpoint
Decision matrix: evaluate revert vs tenant-pin vs hotpatch based on scope, rollback risk, and data residency constraints
Hotfix branch: cut branch from release candidate, apply targeted prompt/weight-fix or parameter guard
Automated acceptance: run per-tenant smoke tests (latency, token-quality heuristics, sample prompts) against a shadowed replica
Canary-like phased re-enable: open traffic gradually by slice percentages and monitor quality SLOs for 30 minutes per step
Full resolution: lift containment and close incident when all checks pass, publish incident notes and postmortem actions
